units.title: Ethereum mainnet reference and cross-chain deployment parity
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

code.title: Monad: the gcc-built emitter run from the real stack states of PoolManager blocks no mined transaction has entered
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 30 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Lead L-1208. Monad validators certify the words that native x86 code computes. The emitter that writes that code sits in the shipped validator binary, which gcc 15.2.0 built; rpc.monad.xyz and every tracing node run only the interpreter, and the harness of cycles 25 to 30 uses a clang build of the same source. Cycle 30 ran the gcc build's register allocator, both spill paths, pop and push, write_to_final_stack_offsets, block_prologue and the non-literal shift arms in the x86 model on about 15,000 generated Stack states with no wrong word, and showed that mined transactions since v0.16.7 reached mainnet (2026-11-26, block 125,426,597) entered 660 of the PoolManager's 913 compiled blocks. 128 value-computing blocks were never entered, 56 of them with emitted code that changed at v0.16.7 (research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-monad-mined-native-coverage.work/out/notentered-classified.json): the FullMath.mulDiv 512-bit copies (0x5757, 0x57ca, 0x5860, 0x588a, 0x58d6, 0x58db), the large-amount paths of SqrtPriceMath, the 100 percent fee path of SwapMath, the tick clamps, donate, the protocol fee blocks and the hook callbacks. Any account can enter them with one transaction, and all validators run the same gcc build, so a wrong word there would be certified while every RPC answer looks right. What is missing is the input: the model has not seen the Stack states those blocks really produce. The Monad validator package is untrusted data. Cycle 27 left it unpacked under research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/dl (p167 for 0.16.7, p165 for 0.16.5); if that directory is missing, download monad_0.16.7_amd64.deb from https://pkg.category.xyz/ pool/main into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory, check SHA256 3cb9dba5501b61ea3487bd042e2b8d12f871cff0e2e15409210e2cef0f8e81fb, and unpack it with ar, node's zlib.zstdDecompressSync and tar as research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/unzst.js does. Never execute, load or dlopen any file from the package. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. The x86 model is research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/x86emu.py with runvec.py. Cycle 29 added a driver that runs emitter functions of the gcc build in the model and records every asmjit call (research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-literal-folds.work/scripts/emdrv.py), and rebuilt the gcc layout of the Stack object from debug information (research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-register-spill.work). Cycle 30 scripts are in research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-monad-gcc-allocator-model.work/scripts (allocdrv.py, shiftfull.py, shiftvar.py, wfso.py, aorel.py, prologue.py, rodata.py, cmpclang.py, faults.json) and research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-monad-mined-native-coverage.work/scripts (build.sh rebuilds the clang harness bit for bit; classify30.py and analyze30.py map program counters to blocks). Task 1: rebuild the clang harness from source with one added hook that writes, at entry to each compiled PoolManager block and before each instruction's emit call, the virtual stack as the emitter holds it: for every element its locations (literal, general register, AVX register, stack offset), the free register queues, the available stack offsets, min_delta, max_delta and the instruction about to be emitted. The hook only writes a log; it must not change what is emitted, which you show by comparing the emitted bytes with cycle 28's listing. Task 2: for each of the 128 un-entered value-computing blocks, starting with the six FullMath blocks and then the 56 blocks changed at v0.16.7, feed the logged state of every instruction to the gcc model: run the gcc build's emit function for that instruction (mul, mulmod, div, sdiv, addmod, add, sub, shifts, comparisons, dup, swap, push, pop, mload, mstore, jumps and the block exit) from the package text on a Stack laid out as the gcc code reads it, record the asmjit calls, and compare the instruction stream with the clang listing up to a consistent renaming of registers and spill slots. Where the gcc function calls a runtime routine (the 256-bit multiply, divide and mulmod helpers), check the argument registers and the saved live set, and run the runtime routine itself from the package text on a few thousand operands with the mulDiv shapes of tools/opdiff/v4math.py. Task 3: for every block where the streams differ beyond renaming, run both streams in the model on at least 2,000 operand sets (edge words, the FullMath, SqrtPriceMath and SwapMath shapes) and compare every word left on the EVM stack and in memory at block exit with pyevm.py. Report per block: instructions, emit functions exercised, equal or renamed or different, cases run. Task 4: say plainly which emit functions of the gcc build are still not run in the model after this cycle and which of the 128 blocks they sit in. Plant at least five faults (a caller-saved register not saved around a runtime call, a wrong argument order to the mulmod helper, a stale stack offset after a spill, a wrong carry limb, a swapped dup source) and show the comparison catches each. Task 5: if any block writes a word that differs from the clang harness and pyevm.py, name the src/ line that reads it, give the operands, and say what a swap or liquidity change by an ordinary account would gain or lock. If none differs, record blocks, instructions and case counts as cleared. This concerns chain 143 only; say so for the other 20 networks.

The PoolManager keeps its whole settlement ledger in transient storage (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol, src/libraries/Lock.sol, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol), so a delta that survived a reverted frame would let a caller keep a credit it never paid. Cycle 21 left the release archive of commit b72783f under research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-go127-arch.work/dl/nitro-zip, and cycle 23 extracted 53 core/vm and holiman/uint256 functions of the amd64 and arm64 binaries through pclntab into research/network-risk/cycles/023/arbitrum-family.work/raw/amd64-fn and arm64-fn (scripts gobuildinfo.py, disasm.sh, opscan.py and the pcln reader are in its scripts/). If the archive is missing, fetch it again as cycle 21 recorded into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory and check it against research/network-risk/cycles/023/arbitrum-family.work/raw/nitro-binaries.sha256. Never execute, load or dlopen any file from it. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. Cycle 30's models and shim are in research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-nitro-binary-arith-lift.work/scripts (goshim.py, drive.py, models.py, jd.py, symcmp.py, coverage.py, faults.py, calls.py, the emu and pcln directories); its dl/ holds the binaries taken from the Docker Hub layers if it is still on disk. Task 1 (L-1211): in both binaries locate opSload, opSstore, opTload, opTstore and every StateDB method they call (GetState, SetState, GetTransientState, SetTransientState, the transientStorage map Get and Set, the journal append for transientStorageChange and storageChange, RevertToSnapshot and the revert methods of those two journal entry types, and Prepare, which resets transient storage). Compare the function names with go-ethereum v1.17.10 and list Arbitrum-only additions. Run the transient path in the models with the Go map modelled by a small stub for the runtime map calls (mapaccess, mapassign and their swiss map variants; record which runtime symbols you stubbed): sequences of TSTORE and TLOAD over the PoolManager's slot shapes (keccak256(target, currency) delta slots, the count, lock and reserve slots), with snapshots, reverts of an inner frame, nested reverts and a write of an equal value. Compare every read with pyevm.py. Task 2 (L-1210): from coverage.py list by address the instructions cycle 30 left unreached in udivrem, udivremBy1, udivremKnuth, Div, Mod, SMod, SDiv, SRsh, Exp, AddMod, MulMod, reduce4 and Reciprocal of both binaries. Classify each as stack growth (morestack), bounds panic, or arithmetic. For every arithmetic one find the operand shape that reaches it, run it, and say whether FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24-48), SqrtPriceMath or TickMath can produce that shape. Task 3 (L-1205): read opCall, opStaticCall, opDelegateCall, opReturnDataCopy, opReturnDataSize and EVM.Call, StaticCall and DelegateCall in the binaries for their control flow only: the snapshot taken before the callee runs, the revert on error, how gas is given back, the value transfer, and any Arbitrum-only branch (names from pclntab). Compare with v1.17.10 source and say what differs. Do the same for the TxProcessor hooks StartTxHook, GasChargingHook and EndTxHook as far as they can touch state the PoolManager reads. Task 4 (L-1206): read the isCode map path (jumpDests Load and Store, the key it uses and the code hash compare) and say under which key a bitmap is stored and whether two different codes can share one. Task 5: plant at least four faults in in-memory copies (a revert that restores zero in place of the previous value, a journal entry skipped, a snapshot index off by one, a wrong map key limb) and show the checks catch them. Then run by eth_call on Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain, with state overrides, an unlock whose callback writes deltas, lets an inner call revert after more writes, and reads them back; compare with pyevm.py and bracket each batch with web3_clientVersion. Task 6: for anything that differs say which src/ line reads the word and what an ordinary account could gain. If nothing differs, record functions, coverage and case counts as cleared and list what is still unread in the binaries.

Every check of these three networks so far rests on source and on RPC answers. Cycle 30 built a way to run functions of a shipped Go binary in x86-64 and AArch64 models with a Go register ABI shim and used it on Nitro (research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-nitro-binary-arith-lift.work/scripts: goshim.py, drive.py, models.py, jd.py, symcmp.py, coverage.py, faults.py, calls.py, emu and pcln). This theme applies it to the binaries the three networks ship. Polygon is the one go-ethereum fork with an arithmetic cache: bor's core/vm/mulmod_memo.go sits in front of MULMOD, which FullMath.mulDiv calls twice (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 and :48). Avalanche folds storage keys at bit 248 (F-040). Release binaries are untrusted data. Look for: the bsc release that carries Jenner (bnb-chain/bsc release assets, or the published container image), the avalanchego release behind the public endpoints (v1.15.2 at last reading; release tarball or the avaplatform/avalanchego image), and the newest tagged bor release (release assets or the 0xpolygon/bor image). Fetch each into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory and check any published checksum. If a host refuses the download, record the refusal and go on with what you have; do not try another route around a refusal. Never execute, load or dlopen any downloaded file. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. Task 1: for each binary record the Go version, the module versions of the EVM package and of holiman/uint256 from the build info, and compare them with what the public endpoints of chains 56, 43114 and 137 report on the day. List every function of the EVM package (core/vm in bsc and bor, the libevm or coreth core/vm in avalanchego) and of uint256 through pclntab, and compare the names with the tagged source. Name every binary-only function, and for each say whether it holds a cache, a memo or a lookup table that an arithmetic, shift, comparison or jump handler reads. For bor say whether the tagged binary contains the MULMOD memo and from which handler it is reached. Task 2: run the handlers of MULMOD, ADDMOD, MUL, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, EXP, SHL, SHR, SAR, BYTE, SIGNEXTEND and the comparisons from each binary in the model on at least 200,000 cases per binary: edge words, the FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, TickMath and SwapMath shapes of tools/opdiff/v4math.py and the vectors of tools/opdiff/battery.py and targeted.py. If bor's memo is present, run sequences that reuse a modulus, alternate two moduli, and change one limb of the modulus between calls, across at least 100,000 sequence steps. Compare every word with Python integers. Task 3: run the jump destination analysis of each binary on the PoolManager runtime (research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json) and on programs that end inside a PUSH.
